top_signals.title: Brent Holds Above $102 as Iran Talks Stall Over Hormuz Conditions
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices took a dip today amid reports that there was willingness for peace in the Middle East on both sides of the conflict. The dip partially offset gains made earlier in the week, keeping oil benchmarks elevated. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $102.20 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was changing hands for $91.43 per barrel. top_signals.title: Trump, Xi Buy Time on Trade With Truce Extension
top_signals.summary: As US President Donald Trump greeted China's Xi Jinping on Wednesday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that an agreement struck last year by the nations will run an additional two months until Jan. 10. Tyler Kendall reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Canada’s Oil Patch On Track For Biggest M&A Wave In A Decade
top_signals.summary: Nearly a decade ago, the Canadian Oil Patch recorded a major asset sale and consolidation wave as oil majors exited the oil sands in favor of higher margins in U.S. shale oil as well as environmental concerns amid the ESG investing craze.
